# Kuaishou Short-Video Marketing: A Complete Guide for Brands in China
URL: https://www.beyondbordergroup.com/insights/boost-your-brand-in-china-the-ultimate-kuaishou-short-video-marketing-guide
Published: 2024-10-28
Author: Beyond Border Group
Category: Platforms

Kuaishou is a premier short-video platform distinct from Douyin, focusing on audiences in lower-tier cities and rural areas. This guide explores how brands can use live-streaming, influencer partnerships, and localized eCommerce strategies for success in China's social commerce market.

## Understanding Kuaishou's Unique Audience

### Demographic Profile

Kuaishou's users are predominantly from China's lower-tier cities and rural areas, featuring a higher concentration of younger users. Unlike Douyin, which caters to urban youth, Kuaishou's audience values community-centric content and relatable, everyday experiences.

### Engagement Preferences

This demographic prefers raw, authentic content, making Kuaishou a great choice for brands aiming to connect with audiences on a personal level rather than through highly polished ads.

### Spending Patterns

Users in lower-tier cities are active participants in China's eCommerce scene, making Kuaishou an ideal platform for brands seeking loyal, cost-conscious consumers who are highly engaged in online shopping.

## Harnessing Kuaishou's Live Commerce Potential

### Direct Sales with China Livestreaming

Kuaishou is a leader in live-stream eCommerce, where creators can sell products in real time during broadcasts. This live sales model is particularly effective on Kuaishou, with conversion rates up to three to five times higher than Douyin's.

![Kuaishou live commerce interface](/Images/insights/2024/12/kai-live-1024x585.png)

### Building Community Trust

Interactive live streams allow brands to answer questions, showcase products, and address customer concerns directly, building trust with viewers and enhancing conversions.

### Optimizing Stream Timing

Brands should aim to stream during Kuaishou's peak hours, around 10 p.m., to maximize reach and engagement. Scheduling streams in advance helps build anticipation and ensures better visibility.

## Using eCommerce China with Kuaishou's Platform Integrations

### Integration with Major eCommerce Platforms

Kuaishou connects cleanly with top Chinese eCommerce platforms like JD.com, Pinduoduo, and Taobao. This integration makes it easy for brands to guide viewers from video content directly to purchase, supporting a streamlined customer journey.

### Product Links in Video Content

Kuaishou's business accounts allow brands to embed product links directly within videos, making it easy for viewers to purchase without leaving the app.

### Creating Relatable eCommerce Content

Brands focusing on storytelling and relatable content see the best engagement on Kuaishou. Showcasing practical product applications rather than purely promotional content helps foster genuine interest and trust.

## Building China Brand Localization with Certified Business Accounts

### Account Verification Benefits

A certified business account on Kuaishou boosts brand credibility and visibility. Verified accounts come with a "V" badge and access to advanced advertising tools, further establishing brand legitimacy.

### Category-specific Profiles

Business profiles can be categorized for better user targeting, allowing consumers to quickly find relevant brands.

### Additional Features for Enhanced Conversion

Certified accounts gain access to additional features, such as advertising discounts, eCommerce tools, and the option to add links in video descriptions, helping brands drive better results in the competitive Chinese eCommerce space.

## Effective Use of Hashtags and Trend Tracking

### Strategic Hashtag Use

Kuaishou's hashtag system is essential for helping content reach a larger audience. By using trending and relevant hashtags, brands can significantly increase impressions.

![Kuaishou trend tracking interface](/Images/insights/2024/12/kai-trend-1024x585.png)

### Participating in Challenges

Kuaishou's "challenge" feature allows brands to run [campaigns](/grow-in-china/campaigns) with specific themes, encouraging user-generated content and helping organically expand brand awareness.

## Working with China Influencers

### Building Authentic Engagement with China KOLs

Kuaishou's influencers, known as Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs), are trusted figures who offer brands an authentic way to reach their audience. Partnering with KOLs can lead to high sales during special events, such as shopping festivals.

### Choosing the Right Influencer

Brands should carefully select KOLs who resonate with their target demographic and demonstrate a track record of engagement.

### Tracking Campaign Success

Monitoring sales metrics, engagement rates, and viewer feedback ensures that KOL partnerships align with business objectives and deliver effective results.

## Implementing a Localized Content Strategy

### Geo-targeted Advertising

Kuaishou's localized advertising options allow brands to reach specific geographic markets within China, making ads highly relevant to each audience.

### Tailoring Messaging for Rural Audiences

Kuaishou's strong presence in rural areas makes it essential for brands to adapt their messaging to reflect the preferences and lifestyle of lower-tier city consumers, highlighting practical benefits and affordable pricing.

## Enhancing Brand Engagement with Augmented Reality (AR) Tools

### Interactive Filters and AR Environments

Kuaishou's AR capabilities provide brands with the tools to create visually stimulating, interactive content. Filters and virtual environments can make brand experiences more memorable and appealing.

### Immersive Brand Storytelling

Through AR, brands can invite users to explore products in virtual settings, offering experiences like virtual try-ons that boost engagement and appeal to digital-savvy consumers.

## Paid Advertising Solutions on Kuaishou

### Open Screen Ads

These ads, displayed whenever the app opens, offer brands immediate exposure to a broad audience.

### Newsfeed Ads

Embedded within the Discovery page, newsfeed ads present as native content, increasing the likelihood of engagement.

### Hashtag Campaigns and Challenges

Creating branded challenges encourages user interaction, allowing brands to generate organic content while boosting visibility and reach.

## Crafting Engaging, Authentic Content for Kuaishou

### Focus on Relatability

Kuaishou's users appreciate unfiltered, authentic content that reflects real-life experiences. Brands that emphasize everyday use and practicality connect better with the audience.

### Experimenting with Content Formats

From live streams to short-form clips, varying content formats can help brands reach different audience segments and discover what resonates best.

### Demonstrations and Storytelling

Content that demonstrates a product's practical use or shows it in relatable scenarios tends to perform well, resonating with Kuaishou's community-focused audience.

## Monitoring Performance with Kuaishou Analytics

### Key Metrics to Track

Kuaishou provides insights on engagement rates, viewer demographics, and purchasing behaviors, helping brands refine their strategy.

### Adapting Based on Analytics

Regularly reviewing top-performing content and emerging trends ensures that brands can optimize their approach and remain relevant in the dynamic Chinese social commerce landscape.

## Embracing Green Content for Sustainable Branding

### Promoting Sustainability

Kuaishou supports eco-friendly practices, and brands with green initiatives can connect with an audience that values sustainability. Environmentally-conscious content gives brands a competitive edge.

### Appealing to Conscious Consumers

Emphasizing green practices helps brands resonate with Kuaishou's environmentally aware user base, fostering loyalty and engagement.

## Common Pitfalls for Brands to Avoid

- Overly Polished Content: Kuaishou's users prefer authenticity; content that appears overly staged may not perform well.
- Neglecting Engagement: Interaction is key on Kuaishou. Brands should actively engage with users, respond to comments, and foster dialogue to build a loyal audience.
- Ignoring Platform Trends: Staying attuned to trending topics and hashtags on Kuaishou is essential for maintaining visibility and engagement.

## Key Takeaways for Kuaishou Marketing Success

- **Use Livestreaming**: Utilize Kuaishou's strong live-streaming ecosystem to showcase products in real-time, answering questions and building immediate connections with viewers.
- **Focus on China Brand Localization**: Adapting content to the cultural nuances and preferences of Kuaishou's user base is essential for success.
- **Engage with KOLs and Influencers**: Partnering with trusted KOLs helps brands reach audiences with authenticity, a core value of Kuaishou's platform.

## Conclusion

Kuaishou provides a distinct platform for brands in China to engage with audiences through localized content, live streaming, and [influencer marketing](/grow-in-china/influencers-kols). As part of a holistic China branding strategy, Kuaishou offers a powerful means to connect authentically with consumers, especially those in rural and lower-tier cities, where demand for relatable content and eCommerce engagement is rapidly rising. Brands that use Kuaishou's strengths effectively can position themselves for lasting success in China's dynamic digital marketplace.

---
# Boost Your Marketing with the Best Chinese Search Engines in 2024
URL: https://www.beyondbordergroup.com/insights/boost-your-marketing-with-the-best-chinese-search-engines-in-2024
Published: 2024-09-02
Author: Beyond Border Group
Category: Platforms

China's internet ecosystem features distinct search engines that differ from Western platforms. Understanding Baidu, Sogou, Shenma, and other Chinese search engines is crucial for effective marketing in China's market.

## Understanding the Chinese Search Engine Market

The Chinese internet landscape is unique due to government regulations, including the Great Firewall, which blocks access to many international websites and search engines. This has given rise to several domestic search engines that cater specifically to Chinese users. As of 2024, the primary search engines in China include Baidu, Sogou, Shenma, and Haosuo, each with its own strengths and user demographics.

## Importance of Chinese Search Engines in Marketing

Search engines in China play a central role in digital marketing. They not only influence search engine optimization (SEO) strategies but also affect advertising [campaigns](/grow-in-china/campaigns) and consumer behavior. Knowing which search engines to prioritize can significantly impact a marketer's success in reaching Chinese consumers.

## Top Chinese Search Engines for 2024

### 1. Baidu: The Dominant Player

Baidu is often referred to as China's Google. With over 50% of the search engine market share in China, it is the go-to platform for most Chinese internet users. Founded in 2000, Baidu has grown beyond search, offering a wide array of services including AI and various internet-related products.

#### Marketing on Baidu

For marketers, Baidu presents a significant opportunity. However, succeeding on Baidu requires understanding its unique SEO practices. Unlike Google, Baidu still relies heavily on meta keywords and places significant emphasis on simplified Chinese content. Websites hosted on Chinese servers with an Internet Content Provider (ICP) license are preferred in rankings. Additionally, Baidu's search algorithms favor HTTPS, fast loading speeds, and high-quality content.

![Baidu logo and interface](/Images/insights/2024/07/baidu.jpg)

### 2. Sogou: The Search Dog

Sogou, launched in 2004, is the second-largest search engine in China. In 2021, it became a subsidiary of Tencent, a major player in the Chinese tech industry. Sogou is deeply integrated with Tencent's popular apps like WeChat and QQ, making it a valuable tool for reaching a broad audience.

#### Marketing on Sogou

Sogou's SEO practices emphasize original content and site authority. Backlinks are crucial, with quantity often trumping quality. While meta descriptions are less important, title tags play a vital role in search rankings. Sogou's integration with Tencent platforms also allows for smooth marketing opportunities within social media and messaging apps.

![Sogou search engine interface](/Images/insights/2024/07/sougou.jpg)

### 3. Shenma: Mobile-First Approach

Shenma is a joint venture between Alibaba and UC Web, focusing exclusively on mobile search. Given that nearly all Chinese internet users access the web via mobile devices, Shenma's mobile-first approach makes it a critical player in the market.

#### Marketing on Shenma

Shenma's close ties with Alibaba mean that products listed on Alibaba platforms like Taobao and Tmall get priority in search results. This makes Shenma an excellent choice for marketers targeting mobile users and promoting ecommerce products. Optimizing for Shenma involves ensuring that product pages on Taobao or Tmall are well-maintained and SEO-friendly.

![Shenma mobile search engine](/Images/insights/2024/07/shenma2-500x408-1.png)

### 4. Haosuo: The Secure Search Engine

Also known as Qihoo 360 Search, Haosuo is known for its emphasis on security. It holds a significant share of the Chinese search market and is often used by businesses for its strong security features.

#### Marketing on Haosuo

Haosuo's SEO rankings prioritize websites with high authority and trustworthiness. This makes it an excellent platform for B2B marketing. The competition on Haosuo is less intense than on Baidu, often resulting in lower cost-per-click rates for paid ads.

![Haosuo search interface](/Images/insights/2024/07/Haosou.png)

### 5. Youdao: The Translation Giant

Youdao, part of the NetEase family, operates more like an educational platform than a traditional search engine. It is primarily used by younger, high-income individuals and offers strong translation services.

#### Marketing on Youdao

Youdao's unique user base and focus on education make it a niche but valuable platform for marketers. Products and services related to education, learning tools, and international products benefit from Youdao's translation capabilities and user engagement.

![Youdao translation and search platform](/Images/insights/2024/07/youdao1.jpg)

## The Importance of Localized SEO in China

Localized SEO is critical for success in China. Each search engine has unique algorithms and preferences that differ significantly from Western search engines. Understanding these nuances and optimizing your [website](/grow-in-china/website) accordingly can greatly enhance your visibility and reach in the [Chinese market](/enter-china/market-entry-consulting).

### Key Elements of Localized SEO

* Language and Content: Use simplified Chinese and create content that resonates with local audiences.
* Hosting and Speed: Host your website on Chinese servers and ensure fast loading times.
* Keywords and Metadata: Utilize meta keywords and alt texts, particularly for Baidu.

## Conclusion

Choosing the best Chinese search engine for your marketing efforts in 2024 depends on your specific goals and target audience. Baidu remains the dominant force, but platforms like Sogou, Shenma, and Haosuo offer unique advantages that can be used for specialized marketing strategies. By understanding the strengths of each search engine and tailoring your approach accordingly, you can effectively reach and engage with the vast Chinese market.

---
# Brand Localization for China: Adapt & Keep Your DNA
URL: https://www.beyondbordergroup.com/insights/brand-localization-for-china-without-losing-your-dna
Published: 2025-11-19
Author: Beyond Border Group
Category: Brand & Localization

Foreign brands in China must balance deep localization with core identity. Quality alone is no longer enough; success requires cultural relevance and platform fluency while protecting what makes the brand distinctive.

## How The Game Has Changed

For a long time, foreign brands stood for rarity and modern life. If it came from overseas, it felt a step ahead.

As the middle class grew, [global brands](/enter-china/market-entry-consulting) became shorthand for status and quality. Domestic brands were still catching up on product, design, and storytelling.

Today, Chinese brands have largely closed the quality gap and often move faster on culture and digital. Guochao has given local players a strong story, and Western brands have become one choice among many. Quality is assumed. Relevance comes from cultural fit and platform fluency.

## Why Localization Is A Must

Two forces make deep [localization](/enter-china/branding-localisation) essential in China.

**1. Quality is a starting line**

Chinese consumers still trust many Western brands for safety and engineering, but domestic brands have raised the bar.

If your main story in China is that you are high quality and international, you are competing with yesterday's expectations.

To stand out now, you need to signal:

- You understand local needs and use cases
- You respect local taste and aesthetics
- You can communicate naturally inside the Chinese digital culture

**2. Content is the store**

Discovery, consideration, and purchase often happen in one continuous digital environment.

For many categories, the journey looks more like:

- Discover on **Douyin** or **Xiaohongshu**
- Validate through notes, comments, and social proof
- Convert through live stream, mini program, or e-commerce flagship

If your brand looks and sounds out of place in those feeds, it does not matter how strong your heritage is. It gets ignored.

Localization is no longer about translating a website. It is about rebuilding how your brand lives inside this content commerce loop.

![](/Images/insights/2025/11/localization-2-1024x576.png)

## What It Looks Like When Brands Get It Right [Apple & Coca-Cola]

The brands that succeed in China do not abandon who they are. They protect their core and flex everything around it.

**Apple keeps:**

- A minimalist, premium visual language
- Creativity-focused storytelling
- A clear and familiar product ecosystem

**Apple adapts in China by:**

- Building campaigns around Chinese festivals and e-commerce peaks
- Running tailored live sessions on platforms like Tmall
- Shaping offers for the Chinese middle class's spending habits

The Apple feeling is unchanged. The route from attention to purchase is very Chinese.

**Coca-Cola keeps:**

- The global promise of happiness and togetherness
- Iconic red, the logo, and the bottle silhouette

**Coca-Cola adapts in China by:**

- Using the Chinese name Kěkǒukělè, which translates as tasty fun
- Creating Chinese New Year editions that fit family rituals and gifting
- Collaborating with local artists and letting those designs travel on Chinese social platforms

The result still feels like Coca-Cola, simply expressed through Chinese moments and symbols.

![](/Images/insights/2025/11/localization-3-1024x576.png)

## A Simple Way To Frame Localization For China

A practical lens for global teams is to separate what must stay from what should move.

**Layer 1: the non-negotiable core**

What should be stable across markets:

- Brand purpose and big idea
- Fundamental values such as safety, joy, creativity, and freedom
- Distinctive visual codes, including logo, main colors, and key shapes
- Product truths, the things you reliably do better than others

If you compromise here, you start to look like every other international brand.

**Layer 2: the China design space**

The intentional flex:

- A Chinese name and key phrases with real meaning and memory value
- Cultural references drawn from festivals, cities, and youth scenes
- China only products, flavors, packs, and bundles for local occasions
- Promotion rhythms aligned with moments like six eighteen, eleven eleven, Qixi, and Double twelve

The core question for every adjustment is simple.

Does this express our big idea in a way that makes sense in China, or are we just decorating with cultural symbols?

**Layer 3: platform native execution**

Strategy turns into content and journeys:

- Douyin for short video storytelling and live commerce
- Xiaohongshu for reviews, lifestyle narratives, and community recommendations
- WeChat for membership, service flows, and mini program commerce
- Tmall, JD, and others for flagship ecommerce and peak events

The brand remains the same, but:

- Hooks and first seconds change
- Pacing and editing change
- Information density and on-screen layout change

You are not changing who you are. You are changing how you enter the scroll.

## From Principle To Practice

Seeing China through this three-layer lens is the easy part. The challenge is turning it into daily choices on names, packs, formats, partners, and media. Under pressure, brands tend to either recycle global work or approve local ideas that slowly dilute who they are.

The ones who stay balanced usually have three things:

- A shared view of what is truly non-negotiable in the brand
- Clear, creative, and experienced territories for China
- A map of real platform journeys, so content follows how people actually move from seeing to buying

This is where Beyond Border Group works with teams, connecting a protected core to a Chinese expression that can stretch without losing itself.

---
# China 2026: 8 eCommerce & Marketing Predictions
URL: https://www.beyondbordergroup.com/insights/china-2026-8-ecommerce-marketing-predictions
Published: 2026-01-02
Author: Cyril Drouin
Category: Market Strategy

Eight predictions for China's digital marketplace in 2026, from instant commerce dominance to GenAI-driven personalization and the resurgence of experiential marketing over discounting.

**From instant commerce to GenAI overload, here's what's coming in China's digital marketplace**

After two decades navigating China's digital ecosystem, I've learned that predicting the future here isn't about crystal balls. It's about connecting the dots between what's already happening in Shanghai's startup districts and what multinational boardrooms will be discussing twelve months from now.

Here's what I see coming in 2026.

## Instant Commerce Will Eat Traditional eCommerce's Lunch

The 30-minute delivery war is just getting started. What I'm calling "instant commerce" (即时零售, jishi lingshou) will aggressively steal market share from traditional [eCommerce](/grow-in-china/cross-border-ecommerce) platforms in 2026.

Meituan (美团) already processes over 2 billion instant delivery orders annually. Ele.me (饿了么) has expanded beyond food to beauty, pharma, and consumer electronics.

> The convenience addiction is real, and there's no going back once you've experienced it.

Tmall (天猫) and JD.com (京东) are racing to build competing infrastructure, but they're retrofitting systems built for next-day delivery, not 30-minute fulfillment. High-frequency purchases like skincare, supplements, and household essentials will migrate to platforms built for speed from day one.

## The Real Human Premium: KOLs and KOCs Become Gold

Here's the paradox GenAI creates: as synthetic content floods Xiaohongshu/RED (小红书), Weibo (微博), and Douyin (抖音), authentic human voices become exponentially more valuable.

I'm watching brands scramble to lock in long-term relationships with proven KOLs and KOCs before their rates skyrocket. The economics are straightforward: when every brand can generate thousands of AI [influencer](/grow-in-china/influencers-kols) posts for pennies, the humans who can move purchase intent become strategic assets.

> Expect KOL fees to increase 30-50% in 2026 for creators who can demonstrate genuine community trust and conversion metrics.

But here's the catch: identifying genuinely human content will become increasingly difficult. Platforms will need verification systems, and consumers will develop their own authenticity filters.

## Performance Marketing Gets Hyper-Personalized at Scale

GenAI's real power in China won't be creating generic content. It will be creating hundreds of personalized ad variants targeting dozens of distinct consumer personas, all within the same media budget.

I've already seen pilot campaigns running 50+ creative variants simultaneously across Tmall, JD, Douyin, WeChat (微信), and Xiaohongshu, each optimized for micro-segments defined by behavioral data.

> In 2026, this becomes standard practice. The technical barrier to entry is low, but the strategic execution complexity is high.

The winning brands will be the ones that master prompt engineering and creative systematisation. Budget size is no longer the deciding factor.

## Experiential Marketing Fills the Discount Fatigue Gap

Chinese consumers are exhausted by the endless discount cycle. Price wars, flash sales, shopping festival promotions. It's all become white noise.

This creates massive opportunity for experiential marketing: pop-up stores with immersive brand storytelling, interactive installations that create shareable moments, community events that build genuine emotional connection, and limited-edition collaborations with local artists.

> The brands that invest in memorable experiences instead of leaning on margin-crushing discounts will build the loyalty that holds up in 2026.

But here's the reality check: experiential marketing requires upfront investment with harder-to-measure ROI. In a market obsessed with immediate performance metrics, convincing stakeholders will be the bigger challenge than executing the experiences themselves.

## Media Costs Hit a Ceiling (Because They Have To)

Media costs on eCommerce platforms will increase only marginally in 2026, despite growing demand. Why? Simple economics.

Sellers are already operating on razor-thin margins. Average net margins for Tmall merchants hover around 3-8%. They literally cannot afford steeper advertising costs without destroying their business models entirely.

> The constraint isn't platform greed. It's merchant economics hitting fundamental limits.

Platforms like Tmall and JD understand this calculation. Push media costs too high, and merchants flee to alternative channels or fold entirely. Expect modest single-digit increases rather than the double-digit jumps we saw in 2019-2021.

## China Becomes Attractive Again for European Niche Brands

I'm seeing a significant shift in cross-border sentiment. The US market, once the promised land for European brands, has become prohibitively complicated: tariffs have killed deal economics for many categories, salary inflation makes building US teams unaffordable for mid-sized brands, logistics costs have increased 40-60% since 2020, and market saturation dominates many premium categories.

> China and Southeast Asia are emerging as the viable alternative, especially for niche and premium European brands.

Does this mean China is easy? Absolutely not. Regulatory uncertainty remains real. The "cheapest wins" procurement mentality still dominates many categories. Local competition is fierce and well-funded.

But the relative economics have shifted. China's cross-border infrastructure, logistics sophistication, and existing frameworks suddenly look attractive when compared to US [market entry](/enter-china/market-entry-consulting) costs in 2026.

## Xiaohongshu and Douyin Dominate Brand-Building

In 2026, Xiaohongshu and Douyin will be the primary channels for marketing and branding campaigns. The integration between Xiaohongshu and Tmall will become critical for conversion.

I see this connection strengthening throughout the year as both platforms recognize the symbiotic value. Xiaohongshu drives discovery and consideration. Tmall captures transaction.

> The brands that master this handoff will massively outperform those treating social and commerce as separate silos.

The playbook: authentic content on Xiaohongshu builds desire, smooth links enable one-tap purchase on Tmall, post-purchase content creation feeds back into the discovery loop.

## Shopping Festivals Lose Their Magic (Except for Launches)

Singles' Day, 6.18, and other shopping festivals will continue their slow decline in strategic importance. Shoppers now expect discounts but don't get particularly excited about them. The magic is gone, and the GMV growth numbers prove it.

However, these festivals remain valuable for one thing: launching new brands. The concentrated traffic across all platforms creates a legitimate window to introduce products to massive audiences.

> Smart brands treat festivals as launch platforms, not as quarterly growth drivers. Adjust expectations accordingly.

---

**Here's the uncomfortable truth: most Western brands are still operating with a 2023 playbook in a market that's already living in 2026. These aren't speculative trends, they're patterns already playing out in tier-one cities right now.**

The brands winning in China aren't the ones with the biggest budgets or the most famous names. They're the ones willing to move at China's speed, embrace technologies their legal departments are still reviewing, and understand that yesterday's best practices are today's commodities.

If your China strategy still looks the same as it did two years ago, you're not standing still. You're falling behind.

---
# China E-Commerce 2025: The Platform Map, and Why Retail Is Going Local
URL: https://www.beyondbordergroup.com/insights/china-e-commerce-platforms-2025
Published: 2025-12-22
Author: Beyond Border Group
Category: E-Commerce

China's e-commerce market integrates online and offline into one operational loop across distinct platforms. Each major player owns different consumer habits and parts of the sales funnel.

## China's e-commerce market keeps setting the reference point. The reason is integration, not size.

The key change for retail is simple: online and offline are converging into one operational loop. Discovery, conversion, fulfilment, and service are increasingly designed as one journey, often inside a single app.

China also has the user base to sustain this integration. The country had more than 1.12 billion internet users as of June 2025.

---

## The platform map

China's major commerce [platforms](/learn-china/platforms) have distinct strengths. Most brands end up operating across several at once because each platform owns a different part of the funnel.

### **Alibaba (Taobao, Tmall, 1688)**

* Taobao and Tmall anchor marketplace commerce at scale (C2C and B2C).
* 1688 supports domestic wholesale and sourcing (B2B), often relevant for manufacturers and distributors.

### **JD.com**

* JD continues to position around logistics reliability and quality control.
* JD reported its annual active customer base surpassed 700 million in October 2025.

### **Pinduoduo (PDD)**

* Pinduoduo remains defined by value and social shopping mechanics, with deep reach beyond top tier cities.

### **Douyin e-commerce**

* Douyin is the clearest example of content and commerce collapsing into one interface.
* Reported RMB 3.5 trillion GMV in 2024 shows the scale of in-app conversion.

### **Kuaishou e-commerce**

* Kuaishou remains a live commerce heavyweight, with deep penetration outside tier 1 cities and a strong community dynamic.

### **Xiaohongshu (RED)**

* RED is still the primary trust engine for many lifestyle categories, driven by UGC and peer validation.
* It is reported at 300M+ monthly active users.

### **Meituan**

* Meituan is a local commerce infrastructure: food delivery, local services, and increasingly instant retail.
* It is reported to hold around 70% of China's food delivery market share.

### **Vipshop**

* Vipshop stays focused on discount retail for branded goods, operating like a rolling outlet model.

![](/Images/insights/2025/12/new-app-2.png)

---

## The big shift: e-commerce is getting physical again

If you want one trend that explains 2025, it is instant commerce.

Instant commerce is not "delivery" as a feature. It is a new retail expectation built on nearby inventory, local fulfilment, and app-native routing. It changes what consumers consider normal for daily goods.

Instant commerce retail sales will reach RMB 1.003 trillion in 2025, with growth outpacing total retail ecommerce.

**This is where online and offline integration becomes structural:**

* Stores behave like mini warehouses.
* Delivery fleets behave like retail infrastructure.
* Apps behave like a local operating system, not a national catalogue.

---

## What this means for global brands in China

[Global brands](/enter-china/market-entry-consulting) do not enter "China [e-commerce](/grow-in-china/cross-border-ecommerce)" as a single channel. They enter a platform system where each player owns a different consumer habit.

**A practical way to think about it is by capability, not by logo:**

* Marketplace scale and search intent: Alibaba ecosystem, JD.
* Content-led conversion: Douyin, Kuaishou.
* Trust-led discovery: Xiaohongshu.
* Local fulfilment and services: Meituan, and the broader instant retail push.

![](/Images/insights/2025/12/new-app-3.png)

---
# China Is No Longer One Market: Why Local Bets Beat National Plans
URL: https://www.beyondbordergroup.com/insights/china-is-no-longer-one-market-a-localized-growth-strategy-for-2025
Author: Beyond Border Group
Category: Market Strategy

Chinese consumers are more deliberate and domestic competition stronger, making the old national playbook obsolete. Winning brands now ask where they deserve to matter locally rather than how to win all of China.

## China Is No Longer One Market: Why Local Bets Beat National Plans

If you work with China day to day, you can feel it. The old growth [playbook](/work) is fading.

For years, many [global brands](/enter-china/market-entry-consulting) treated China as one big growth machine. Pick a hero SKU, choose a celebrity, roll out nationally, and let scale do the work. In a fast-growing market, that could still deliver.

In 2025, it is more likely to expose your weaknesses.

Slower growth, more cautious consumers, and stronger domestic competition mean the old playbook no longer fits. Brands that still chase a single national answer can spend heavily and still struggle to matter.

### From national messages to local relevance

Post Covid, Chinese consumers are more deliberate. They compare, they wait, and they are less willing to pay for the logo alone. At the same time, pride in domestic brands has grown, especially in EVs, beauty, and sportswear.

A one-size-fits-all message now feels blunt.

Winning brands no longer ask "How do we win China?" They ask, "Where do we deserve to matter, and why?"

That means moving away from symbolic [localisation](/enter-china/branding-localisation) and toward structural choices about where and how to show up:

* Choosing specific cities and clusters instead of a single national launch.
* Building activation plans around real local routines, instead of landmarks and clichés.
* Designing creatives that speak to lived experiences, instead of generic cultural references.

When a luxury house invests in a Chengdu experience built around the city's cultural confidence, or a sports brand refurbishes local courts instead of staging a one-off show, it is making exactly this shift. It is not trying to talk to all of China; it is choosing one place and getting it right.

![](/Images/insights/2024/06/localization-1-1024x576.png)

### China has many markets, not one

Domestic brands understand this.

Many grow through tightly targeted tests: one city, one platform, one festival, one micro segment. Some initiatives are never meant to scale nationally. They exist to build depth or to learn what truly resonates.

For global brands, this can feel uncomfortable. It cuts against habits from other markets, where efficiency and national reach are primary goals.

In today's China, that mindset is risky.

Treating China as a single market often leads to:

* Over-reliance on tier one cities like Shanghai, where competition and media costs are highest.
* Platform plans that follow headline user numbers, not local usage and content cultures.
* Creative that leans on safe symbols like pandas and the Great Wall, instead of real-life insight.

Meanwhile, Gen Z in lower-tier cities may have comparable spending power in certain categories, fewer competing messages, and more time to engage with content. The opportunity is there, but only for brands willing to design for it.

### A portfolio of local bets, not one big gamble

There is no longer such a thing as "winning China" with a single strategy.

What works instead is a portfolio of local bets, some big, some small, some that quietly end. This is how many successful domestic brands already operate, and it is increasingly how foreign brands will need to think.

A practical portfolio might include:

* 2 to 3 priority city clusters, each with its own role, audience focus, and media mix.
* Platform strategies that follow behaviour, for example, Douyin and Xiaohongshu in coastal tier ones, and other platforms in specific inland regions.
* A mix of national tentpole moments and city-level experiments around local life, from sports courts and food streets to campus and community events.
* Product and offer tests are designed to learn fast, not to become instant national rollouts.

This approach is more complex, but more honest about how China behaves as a market.

### What global teams need to change

For leadership teams outside China, the hardest shift is often organisational, not creative.

Three changes matter:

* Measure depth as well as reach. A Chengdu activation that moves local preference can be more valuable than a national burst that leaves shallow impressions.
* Give local teams more room. Deep localisation needs people close to platforms, culture, and retail. Central teams should set guardrails, not dictate every move.
* Fund learning, not just launches. Some ideas will not scale, and that is fine. The point is whether each test sharpens your sense of where the brand truly has the right to win.

The brands that adapt fastest will be those that treat China less like a single line on a spreadsheet and more like a set of evolving opportunities.

![](/Images/insights/2024/06/localization-2-1-1024x647.png)

### Turning Insight Into Action With BBG

At BBG, we work with global brands that feel this shift in China and need a concrete way to respond.

We help teams move from single national plans to structured portfolios of China bets. That can include city and cluster strategy, platform roadmaps across Douyin, Xiaohongshu, WeChat, Tmall, JD, and others, and localisation of brand and commerce experiences that still respect global DNA.

The goal is simple. Less chasing abstract "China scale", more building specific relevance where your brand can genuinely stand out.

# China Is No Longer One Market: Why Local Bets Beat National Plans
URL: https://www.beyondbordergroup.com/insights/china-is-no-longer-one-market-why-local-bets-beat-national-plans
Published: 2026-01-06
Author: Beyond Border Group
Category: Market Strategy

Global brands must shift from single national strategies to localized, city-level approaches to succeed in today's slower-growth Chinese market where domestic competition is stronger.

If you work with China day to day, you can feel it. The old growth [playbook](/work) is fading.

For years, many [global brands](/enter-china/market-entry-consulting) treated China as one big growth machine. Pick a hero SKU, choose a celebrity, roll out nationally, and let scale do the work. In a fast-growing market, that could still deliver. In 2025, it is more likely to expose your weaknesses. Slower growth, more cautious consumers, and stronger domestic competition mean the old playbook no longer fits. Brands that still chase a single national answer can spend heavily and still struggle to matter.

## From national messages to local relevance

Post Covid, Chinese consumers are more deliberate. They compare, they wait, and they are less willing to pay for logo alone. At the same time, pride in domestic brands has grown, especially in EVs, beauty, and sportswear.

A one-size-fits-all message now feels blunt.

Winning brands no longer ask "How do we win China?". They ask "Where do we deserve to matter, and why?"

That means moving away from symbolic [localisation](/enter-china/branding-localisation) and toward structural choices about where and how to show up:

- Choosing specific cities and clusters instead of a single national launch.
- Building activation plans around real local routines, instead of landmarks and clichés.
- Designing creatives that speak to lived experiences, instead of generic cultural references.

When a luxury house invests in a Chengdu experience built around the city's cultural confidence, or a sports brand refurbishes local courts instead of staging a one off show, it is making exactly this shift. It is not trying to talk to all of China; it is choosing one place and getting it right.

![](/Images/insights/2024/06/localization-1-1024x576.png)

---

## China has many markets, not one

Domestic brands understand this.

Many grow through tightly targeted tests: one city, one platform, one festival, one micro segment. Some initiatives are never meant to scale nationally. They exist to build depth or to learn what truly resonates.

For global brands, this can feel uncomfortable. It cuts against habits from other markets, where efficiency and national reach are primary goals.

In today's China, that mindset is risky.

Treating China as a single market often leads to:

- Over-reliance on tier one cities like Shanghai, where competition and media costs are highest.
- Platform plans that follow headline user numbers, not local usage and content cultures.
- Creative that leans on safe symbols like pandas and the Great Wall, instead of real-life insight.

Meanwhile, Gen Z in lower-tier cities may have comparable spending power in certain categories, fewer competing messages, and more time to engage with content. The opportunity is there, but only for brands willing to design for it.

---

## A portfolio of local bets, not one big gamble

There is no longer such a thing as "winning China" with a single strategy.

What works instead is a portfolio of local bets, some big, some small, some that quietly end. This is how many successful domestic brands already operate, and it is increasingly how foreign brands will need to think.

A practical portfolio might include:

- 2 to 3 priority city clusters, each with its own role, audience focus, and media mix.
- Platform strategies that follow behaviour, for example, Douyin and Xiaohongshu in coastal tier ones, and other platforms in specific inland regions.
- A mix of national tentpole moments and city-level experiments around local life, from sports courts and food streets to campus and community events.
- Product and offer tests are designed to learn fast, not to become instant national rollouts.

This approach is more complex, but more honest about how China behaves as a market.

---

## What global teams need to change

For leadership teams outside China, the hardest shift is often organisational, not creative.

Three changes matter:

- **Measure depth as well as reach.** A Chengdu activation that moves local preference can be more valuable than a national burst that leaves shallow impressions.
- **Give local teams more room.** Deep localisation needs people close to platforms, culture, and retail. Central teams should set guardrails, not dictate every move.
- **Fund learning as well as launches.** Some ideas will not scale, and that is fine. The point is whether each test sharpens your sense of where the brand has the right to win.

The brands that adapt fastest will be those that treat China less like a single line on a spreadsheet and more like a set of evolving opportunities.

![](/Images/insights/2024/06/localization-2-1-1024x647.png)

---

## Turning Insight Into Action With BBG

At BBG, we work with global brands that feel this shift in China and need a concrete way to respond.

We help teams move from single national plans to structured portfolios of China bets. That can include city and cluster strategy, platform roadmaps across Douyin, Xiaohongshu, WeChat, Tmall, JD and others, and localisation of brand and commerce experiences that still respect global DNA.

The goal is simple. Less chasing abstract "China scale", more building specific relevance where your brand can genuinely stand out.

---
# China Social Media and KOL Strategies for eCommerce Brands
URL: https://www.beyondbordergroup.com/insights/china-social-media-and-kol-strategies-for-ecommerce-brands
Published: 2024-11-28
Author: Beyond Border Group
Category: KOLs & Livestream

Partnering with Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs) has become a powerful way to connect with Chinese consumers. This guide explores strategies for finding and collaborating with the right KOLs to maximize reach, credibility, and brand growth.

## Understanding KOLs and Their Impact on Chinese Consumers

### What is a KOL in China?

A Key Opinion Leader ([KOL](/grow-in-china/influencers-kols)) in China is an influencer with a substantial following who holds significant sway over their audience's opinions and purchasing decisions. Unlike Western influencers, KOLs in China are seen as trusted experts who offer advice and product recommendations across various categories, from beauty and fashion to tech and lifestyle.

### Why KOLs are Essential for Brands in China

The influence of KOLs goes beyond mere visibility. In China, consumers are generally more receptive to product recommendations from familiar online personalities than from traditional advertising. This consumer preference makes KOLs essential partners for brand growth, as they build trust and foster strong connections with their followers, turning them into engaged and loyal customers.

## Platforms to Reach KOLs in China

Understanding the [social media](/grow-in-china/social-commerce) ecosystem in China is crucial for effectively finding KOLs. Unlike the Western world, where platforms like Instagram and YouTube dominate, China has its own unique social media giants.

### Key Social Media Platforms

#### WeChat

Known for its versatility, WeChat is used by KOLs to engage with fans, create exclusive content, and even conduct e-commerce directly within the platform.

![KOL WeChat](/Images/insights/2024/11/kol_wechat-2.jpg)

#### Weibo

Similar to Twitter, Weibo is ideal for content sharing, making it a popular space for influencer marketing, especially for news, entertainment, and product updates.

![KOL Weibo](/Images/insights/2024/11/kol_weibo.jpg)

#### Douyin (TikTok)

As one of the leading short-video platforms, Douyin allows KOLs to showcase products through live streaming and engaging video content.

![KOL Douyin](/Images/insights/2024/11/kol_duoyin.jpg)

#### Xiaohongshu (Little Red Book)

Targeting mainly fashion and beauty enthusiasts, Xiaohongshu is known for its authentic community, where KOLs post product reviews and recommendations.

![KOL Red](/Images/insights/2024/11/kol_red.jpg)

## How to Find the Right KOLs for Your Brand

Finding the right KOL requires a strategic approach to align with your brand goals and target audience. A few essential considerations can guide your search and help you make informed choices.

### Step 1: Define Your Objectives

* Increase Brand Awareness: For new brands or products, look for KOLs with a broad reach and high visibility.
* Drive Engagement and Sales: If your primary aim is sales, micro-KOLs with engaged followers may yield better results, as they tend to foster a more personal relationship with their audience.
* Build Credibility and Trust: For long-term brand building, work with KOLs whose content style aligns with your brand ethos and values.

### Step 2: Choose the Right Platforms

The choice of platform plays a significant role in influencer effectiveness. Each platform has its audience demographics and engagement levels, so matching your platform choice with your brand's audience is key.

### Step 3: Use KOL Discovery Tools

Several online tools are available to help brands identify and analyze KOLs:

* Yourank.cn: Provides analytics on KOLs, helping you evaluate potential candidates based on metrics like engagement rate and follower demographics.
* Newrank.cn: Offers a detailed database of influencers on multiple platforms, making it easier to find suitable KOLs across categories.
* WeMedia: While affordable, this platform requires careful selection, as it includes both established and emerging influencers.

## Types of KOLs in China

Understanding the different types of influencers in China can help you choose the right partner based on your budget, goals, and brand image.

### Mega-Celebrities

These are actors, musicians, and other public figures with massive followings, typically suited for luxury brands or large [campaigns](/grow-in-china/campaigns). They come at a high cost but can provide extensive reach.

### KOLs (Macro Influencers)

Specialists in a particular niche, KOLs work with brands across a specific industry, making them valuable for brands looking for targeted influence within a particular market segment.

### Micro-KOLs

These influencers generally have fewer followers but more intimate and engaged relationships with their audience. For brands with smaller budgets, micro-KOLs can be a cost-effective way to reach highly engaged communities.

### Key Opinion Consumers (KOCs)

Regular consumers with a strong online presence, KOCs offer authentic product reviews and recommendations. They are especially popular with brands aiming for grassroots marketing and customer trust.

## Strategies for Effective KOL Partnerships in China

Partnering with KOLs effectively involves several strategies tailored to optimize reach, engagement, and return on investment.

### Start with a Small Campaign

If new to the Chinese market, consider starting with a small campaign involving micro-KOLs or KOCs to test market response. This approach is cost-effective and allows you to gauge the success of your messaging before investing heavily.

### Mix Different Types of KOLs

For maximum reach and influence, a mix of KOLs can be beneficial. For instance, pairing a mega-celebrity for reach with a few micro-KOLs for engagement can help create a comprehensive campaign.

### Focus on Authentic Content

Chinese consumers value authenticity. Encourage KOLs to create genuine, relatable content instead of overly polished ads. Live streaming, for instance, is a popular method where influencers provide real-time product demonstrations and engage with their followers.

### Engage with Multiple Platforms

China's digital ecosystem thrives on cross-platform engagement. By using multiple KOLs across platforms like Douyin, Xiaohongshu, and Weibo, you can create a broader impact, reaching audiences in different spaces.

### Budget for KOL Campaigns

Costs can vary widely depending on the KOL's reach and popularity. Major KOLs may charge anywhere from thousands to millions of dollars per campaign, while micro-KOLs are generally more affordable. Budgeting well for KOL partnerships can maximize your campaign's impact.

## Navigating Potential Challenges in KOL Marketing

### Avoiding Fake KOLs

One of the main challenges in the Chinese KOL market is distinguishing between genuine influencers and fake KOLs, who often inflate follower numbers through bots. Platforms like Yourank.cn offer analytics that can help you verify KOL authenticity and engagement rates.

### Managing High Costs

KOLs, particularly mega-celebrities, can be expensive, so understanding the pricing model is crucial. Brands new to China should consider micro-KOLs to manage costs effectively while building brand presence.

### Cultural Sensitivity and Alignment

Ensuring that your brand's values and messaging align with Chinese cultural norms is essential. Work with KOLs who resonate with Chinese audiences and who understand the nuances of promoting products in a culturally sensitive way.

## Measuring the Success of Your KOL Campaign

Evaluating the performance of a KOL campaign is crucial to understanding its impact and planning future strategies.

### Track Engagement Metrics

Views, likes, shares, and comments are all important metrics to gauge the effectiveness of your campaign.

### Analyze Sales Conversions

Many platforms offer in-app purchasing features that make it easy to track conversions directly linked to influencer promotions.

### Measure Brand Sentiment

Monitoring social media sentiment and comments can provide insights into how your brand is perceived post-campaign.

## Conclusion

Finding and partnering with KOLs in China can be a transformative strategy for brands seeking to expand their reach and build trust in one of the world's largest markets. By understanding the types of influencers, choosing the right platforms, and implementing tailored strategies, brands can successfully use the power of Chinese KOLs to create meaningful connections with consumers. Whether you're a global brand or a niche company, aligning with the right KOLs can help elevate your brand's influence, drive sales, and establish a long-term presence in China's competitive market.

---
# China's AI-Powered Commerce: Trends and Innovations to Watch
URL: https://www.beyondbordergroup.com/insights/chinas-ai-powered-commerce-trends-and-innovations-to-watch
Published: 2025-01-10
Author: Beyond Border Group
Category: AI & Innovation

China has rapidly integrated AI technology into marketing and commerce sectors, using platforms like Alibaba and JD.com to revolutionize customer experiences, e-commerce, and retail operations across the nation.

## AI-Powered Marketing Innovations

Chinese companies and digital [marketing](/grow-in-china/campaigns) agencies in China are leading the way in revolutionizing marketing strategies with AI. Platforms like Alibaba and JD.com use AI to offer personalized customer experiences, optimize campaigns, and enhance consumer engagement.

Key applications in marketing include:

- **Personalized Recommendations:** Advanced algorithms analyze consumer data to provide tailored product suggestions, boosting conversion rates.
- **Dynamic Pricing Models:** AI adjusts prices in real time based on demand, competition, and customer behavior.
- **Chatbots and Virtual Assistants:** AI-powered assistants improve customer interactions by providing instant support and personalized shopping guidance.

![](/Images/insights/2025/01/virtual-avatar-by-Alibaba-Group-1024x576.png)

Source: Alibaba Group

These advancements have enabled media agencies in China to help brands achieve new heights in consumer-centric marketing, setting global standards.

## AI in E-Commerce

[E-commerce](/grow-in-china/cross-border-ecommerce) in China has been transformed by AI technologies, creating unparalleled user experiences. Ecommerce agencies in China utilize tools like machine learning and natural language processing to streamline operations and improve customer satisfaction.

### Key Advancements in E-Commerce

- **Visual Search Technology:** Platforms allow users to search for products using images, making online shopping more intuitive.
- **Augmented Reality (AR) Shopping:** AI-powered AR tools help customers visualize products in real-world settings, such as trying on clothes virtually.
- **Fraud Detection:** AI algorithms identify fraudulent transactions, ensuring secure shopping experiences.

As AI advances, crossborder e-commerce in China is becoming more efficient, allowing global brands to connect smoothly with Chinese consumers.

## AI's Impact on Social Commerce

Social commerce is a booming sector in China, with platforms like WeChat and Douyin integrating AI to analyze user behavior. AI-driven tools help creative agencies in China craft hyper-targeted campaigns that resonate with specific audiences.

![](/Images/insights/2025/01/livestream-Douyin_2-300x198.png)

### AI Applications in Social Commerce

- **Content Personalization:** AI ensures users see ads and products that align with their preferences.
- **Livestream Shopping:** AI enhances live shopping experiences by providing real-time analytics and interaction tools.
- **[Influencer](/grow-in-china/influencers-kols) Marketing:** Algorithms identify suitable influencers for brands, maximizing campaign impact.

These developments empower social media agencies in China to create innovative marketing strategies, redefining how products are discovered and sold.

## Smart Retail: Bridging Online and Offline

AI is bridging the gap between online and offline retail in China, creating smarter shopping experiences. Marketing agencies in China are using AI to design smarter store layouts, improve inventory management, and provide smooth checkout solutions.

### Examples of Smart Retail Applications

- **Facial Recognition Payments:** AI-powered systems allow for smooth, contactless transactions.
- **Inventory Management:** Predictive analytics help retailers forecast demand, minimizing waste and ensuring stock availability.
- **Personalized In-Store Experiences:** AI enhances the physical shopping journey with customized offers and suggestions.

By integrating these solutions, digital agencies in China are helping businesses align with the evolving retail landscape.

## Generative AI in Advertising and Content Creation

Generative AI tools like Baidu's Ernie model are transforming how content is created. Advertising agencies in China use these tools to produce high-quality advertisements, videos, and promotional content at scale.

### Benefits of Generative AI in Marketing

#### Cost Efficiency

Automates repetitive tasks, freeing resources for strategic initiatives.

#### Creativity Enhancement

Produces innovative ad designs and content tailored to target audiences.

#### Multilingual Capabilities

Supports global campaigns by generating content in multiple languages.

Generative AI is empowering brands to innovate faster, maintain relevance, and deliver high-quality marketing materials.

## AI in Logistics and Supply Chain Management

China's commerce ecosystem relies on AI to enhance logistics and supply chain efficiency. Companies like JD Logistics utilize AI-powered systems to predict delivery times and minimize inefficiencies, often collaborating with ecommerce agencies in China to streamline operations.

### AI Applications in Logistics

- **Route Optimization:** AI determines the fastest delivery routes, reducing transit times.
- **Warehouse Automation:** Robotic systems manage inventory with precision, improving fulfillment speed.
- **Demand Forecasting:** Algorithms predict consumer demand, enabling proactive inventory management.

These advancements have significantly improved delivery speed and accuracy, making Chinese logistics a global standard.

## Ethical Challenges and Data Privacy Concerns

The rapid integration of AI in commerce raises important ethical and privacy concerns. With extensive data collection practices, China faces challenges in balancing innovation with consumer rights. Media agencies in China must navigate these issues carefully to maintain public trust.

To address these issues, the government has introduced regulations like the Data Security Law, mandating transparency and accountability in AI applications. Balancing innovation with ethical considerations remains a key challenge for China's AI ecosystem.

## The Global Influence of China's AI Ecosystem

China's AI advancements are influencing global commerce, with its innovations being adopted worldwide. From smart cities to crossborder ecommerce in China, the country's solutions are shaping international markets.

### Exporting AI Solutions

- **Smart Cities:** AI-powered urban management tools are improving global infrastructure.
- **Fintech Solutions:** China's AI-driven financial platforms are setting international standards.
- **AI-Powered Marketing Tools:** Innovations like real-time analytics are being integrated into global campaigns.

The contributions of branding agencies in China and other firms demonstrate the international significance of China's AI ecosystem.

## Future Outlook for AI in Chinese Marketing and Commerce

China's marketing and commerce landscape will continue to evolve with AI at its core. Agencies such as media buying agencies in China and digital marketing agencies in China will play key roles in advancing hyper-personalized campaigns and immersive shopping experiences.

- **Hyper-Personalized Marketing:** AI will refine customer segmentation, delivering even more precise campaigns.
- **Expanded AR/VR Integration:** Immersive shopping experiences will redefine consumer engagement.
- **Sustainable AI Solutions:** Companies will adopt eco-friendly AI practices to meet global demands.

As AI technology advances, China's marketing and commerce sectors will remain at the forefront of innovation, shaping the global economy.

## Conclusion

China's advancements in AI are revolutionizing the marketing and commerce landscape. With strong government support, innovative companies, and advanced research, the nation has become a global AI powerhouse. From personalized marketing to efficient logistics, AI's transformative impact is evident across all aspects of commerce.

As China continues to lead the way, the collaboration between government, academic institutions, and agencies like branding agencies in China will drive further innovation. These advancements not only benefit industries and consumers but also position China as a global AI powerhouse shaping the future of commerce.

# China's eCommerce Evolution Driven by Tech, Beauty, and Luxury Sales
URL: https://www.beyondbordergroup.com/insights/chinas-consumer-trends-in-tech-beauty-and-luxury-insights-from-6-18-sales
Published: 2024-06-14
Author: Beyond Border Group
Category: E-Commerce

China's 6.18 shopping festival revealed significant shifts in consumer preferences, with tech, beauty, and luxury brands achieving record sales figures through strategic marketing and dynamic commerce strategies.

## China's Consumer Landscape and Market Shifts

China's consumer landscape is rapidly evolving, with significant shifts in preferences and spending patterns. Recent sales data from Alibaba's Taobao and [Tmall](/grow-in-china/cross-border-ecommerce) during the 6.18 shopping festival reveal these changes vividly, showcasing strong demand across tech, beauty, and luxury segments.

## Tech Products Dominate Early Sales

The 6.18 shopping festival, one of China's largest, saw a remarkable surge in tech product sales. Apple's Tmall store alone achieved a gross merchandise value (GMV) of over RMB1.5 billion within the first hour on May 20. This surge was echoed by other smartphone brands like Huawei and Xiaomi, which reported GMV exceeding RMB100 million.

Home appliances also saw a significant uptick, with brands such as Haier, Gree, and Midea surpassing RMB100 million in GMV within the first hour.

The appeal of these tech products is driven by steep discounts and aggressive marketing strategies, emphasizing the growing consumer appetite for high-quality electronics. These trends show the importance of effective eCommerce strategy in China, where brands use online platforms to maximize sales.

## Beauty Brands Shine Bright

Beauty products were another standout category during the 6.18 sales. Within the first 30 minutes, brands like Proya, Lancome, L'Oreal, and Estee Lauder each reported GMV exceeding RMB100 million. This trend shows the strong demand for premium beauty products in China, driven by an increasing focus on personal care and grooming.

Marketing [campaigns](/grow-in-china/campaigns) for these brands often use social media platforms in China, creating an engaging shopping experience that resonates with young, tech-savvy consumers. Discounts and special offers during the festival further incentivized purchases, contributing to the impressive sales figures.

## Luxury Brands Capture Consumer Attention

Luxury brands also performed exceptionally well during the 6.18 sales. Over 200 brands from the world's five largest luxury conglomerates participated, with names like Miu Miu and Valentino surpassing their full-day sales from the previous year within the first hour. This strong performance reflects the strong demand for luxury goods among Chinese consumers, who are increasingly willing to invest in high-end products.

The luxury sector's success can be attributed to targeted marketing campaigns that emphasize exclusivity and prestige. Additionally, the introduction of special discounts and limited-time offers during the festival created a sense of urgency, prompting consumers to make quick purchasing decisions.

![Miu Miu luxury product display](/Images/insights/2024/06/S519-1.avif)

## Evolving Shopping Dynamics

This year's 6.18 festival marked a significant shift in shopping dynamics. Alibaba's decision to forgo a pre-sale period in favor of two shopping windows from May 20 to June 20 altered consumer behavior. The platforms also reintroduced popular in-app sales venues with products at 50% off, alongside traditional discounts and deals, such as RMB50 off every RMB300 spent.

These changes fostered a more immediate and dynamic shopping experience, encouraging consumers to engage more actively with the platforms. The increased visit volume by members of Tmall's 88VIP loyalty program, which rose by 40% year-over-year on the first day of sales, shows this shift. Moreover, the number of members placing orders surged by over 50%, and the average order value increased by over 30%.

## Small Businesses Benefit

Big brands were not the only winners. On the first day alone, 370,000 small businesses saw their GMV double compared to the previous year.

This trend highlights the inclusive nature of the festival, providing a platform for smaller enterprises to reach a broader audience and compete effectively. This aspect of the event showcases the potential for cross-border eCommerce in China, allowing international small businesses to tap into the vast Chinese market.

## Strategic Marketing Drives Success

The success of the 6.18 sales can be largely attributed to strategic marketing efforts. Brands used a mix of digital marketing techniques, including social media campaigns, influencer partnerships, and live streaming events. These strategies helped create buzz and anticipation, driving traffic to e-commerce platforms.

Moreover, personalized marketing, based on consumer data and preferences, played a crucial role. Tailored promotions and recommendations enhanced the shopping experience, making it more relevant and engaging for consumers.

![Marketing strategy advertisement display](/Images/insights/2024/06/ads.jpg)

## Conclusion

The latest sales data from the 6.18 shopping festival offers valuable insights into China's consumer trends. The strong performance of tech, beauty, and luxury brands highlights the evolving preferences and increasing purchasing power of Chinese consumers. By using strategic marketing and dynamic sales strategies, brands can continue to capitalize on these trends, driving growth in one of the world's most lucrative markets.
